claims.text: Each S-GRU layer applies an MLP-generated scalar gate to the frozen Transformer's residual update.
The optimization uses gate-only fine-tuning rather than updating the pretrained backbone.
The training objective adds a mean gate-activation sparsity penalty, weighted by lambda_sparsity, to the language-modeling loss.

claims.text: The paper cautions that dense GPU kernels, kernel-launch overhead, and missing hardware support for conditional branching can make dynamic residual skipping yield negligible wall-clock savings.

method: S-GRU adds a learned scalar MLP gate to each frozen TinyLlama residual block and trains only those gates with a language-modeling-plus-sparsity objective so layers can be bypassed dynamically.
problem: Dense, fixed-depth Transformer language models execute all layers for every input, creating avoidable computational and energy costs.

The source reports experiments on a single NVIDIA RTX 5060 GPU and describes its CUDA configuration as mimicking mobile-SoC processing constraints; it does not report measurements on a physical target edge device.
The 1.31x gain is explicitly labeled theoretical, while the 44.31 ms latency result comes from the constrained RTX setup.
